listenings.text: Hello. Today we have five questions for Marina Alves. What did you study in your project? Where did you go last year? When did the project start? Why did you choose small schools? And how did you prepare for the visits? Marina answered all of them in the newsletter, and her last answer is the most interesting: she read every report of the last ten years, and then she asked the teachers. Please read the interview before our call. Thank you.

Hi, this is a short message about the questions after your presentation. People usually ask three things. First, where the data comes from. Second, how many schools you visited. And third, why you chose this subject. You do not need a long answer. Two sentences are enough for each question. If somebody asks something you do not know, say: that is a very good question, I do not have the data here. Nobody expects more. Good luck in November.

lesson.grammar_point: wh- questions in the simple past

reading.rtitle: Meteoro Newsletter -- Five Questions for Marina Alves
paras: WHAT did you study in your project? I studied technology in small schools, in the northeast of Brazil.
WHERE did you go last year? I went to eleven schools, in three different states. Two of them were very far from the city.
WHEN did the project start? It started in March 2024, and we finished the first part in December.
WHY did you choose small schools? Because nobody studied them before. And HOW did you prepare? I read every report of the last ten years -- and then I asked the teachers.
